question: A team is spawning an agent team to refactor three independent modules in parallel. Which of the following practices reflect the documented best practices for structuring this agent team? (Select all that apply.)
options: A) Maximize the number of teammates spawned at the start, because more teammates always finish the refactor in proportionally less time.
B) Start with a small number of teammates, such as three to five, and scale up only if the work benefits from more parallel workers.
C) Assign each teammate its own distinct set of files so that no two teammates ever edit the same file at the same time.
D) Break the refactor into enough self-contained tasks that each teammate has roughly five to six tasks to work through.
E) Let every teammate edit any file in the codebase freely so no teammate is ever blocked waiting for a file to become available.
correct_answers: B) Start with a small number of teammates, such as three to five, and scale up only if the work benefits from more parallel workers.
C) Assign each teammate its own distinct set of files so that no two teammates ever edit the same file at the same time.
D) Break the refactor into enough self-contained tasks that each teammate has roughly five to six tasks to work through.
explanations: Incorrect. Adding more teammates does not proportionally reduce refactor time; coordination overhead grows, and returns diminish beyond a certain point.
Correct. Beginning with a small team of three to five and scaling up only when additional parallelism clearly helps is the documented best practice for agent team sizing.
Correct. Giving each teammate a distinct set of files prevents file conflicts and is a documented best practice for parallel agent teamwork.
Correct. Structuring the refactor into self-contained tasks so that each teammate handles about five to six tasks is documented guidance for maintaining productivity.
Incorrect. Allowing all teammates to edit any file freely can cause conflicting overwrites; the best practice is to assign distinct file sets to avoid such conflicts.
